newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains fed cattle market inactive - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains fed cattle market inactive - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle markets were inactive Monday following active sales last week at $66.00 per cwt, up $2.00 from the previous week, feedlot sources said.
Packer bids ranged from $65.00 to $66.00, with owners pricing cattle $68.00 to $70.00, they said.
Fed cattle prices this week were expected buoyed by firm beef prices and the ability of feedlots to remain extremely current in their marketings, the sources said.
Beef prices at midday were quoted up $0.62 to $0.84 per cwt, USDA said.
Heavier-weight choice beef prices at midday were up $0.84 at $100.29, which was $4.68 higher than last Monday's close, USDA statistics showed.

Showlists this week were estimated near 85,000 head in the Texas Panhandle and western Oklahoma area, up 7,500 from last week, market sources said. Kansas showlists were pegged near 68,900 head, down 6,300.
Nebraska showlists were estimated near 73,500 head, up 2,000 from last week, the sources said.
Nebraska cattle traded at $109.00 per cwt on a dressed basis for about 400 head, up $1.00 from last week's top price.
